_comments: S-US9's LOG-ACTIVITY ACTION. Its own file for the same coordination reason as the other two:
MetadataSync reads every dot-json in the directory, so sessions adding a file each conflict on
nothing while two appending to one file conflict always.
WHY THIS ROW HAD TO EXIST AT ALL. The deal-activity pane wrote its own reduced copy of the
activity composition and omitted LoggedByUserID -- NOT NULL with no default on
__mj_BizAppsCommon.Activity -- so logging an activity from the UI failed at the database with a
raw constraint error, every time, for the whole life of the feature. It also wrote the activity
and its link as two independent saves, so a link failure left a committed activity nothing could
The fix was not to add the missing field to the pane. It was to give the pane a way to call the
real composition -- ActivityWriterService, which stamps the field, resolves the deal's parties and
wraps the whole thing in one transaction -- and delete its copy. This row is that way.
AN ACTION RATHER THAN A REMOTE OPERATION, and that is a constraint. Operation shells are CodeGen
output and CodeGen is not run here to close a gap (docs/CODEGEN-PARTIAL-RUNS.md records three
partially-failed runs). An Action needs a metadata row and a @RegisterClass, and is callable from
the browser through GraphQLActionClient.RunAction -- the same path MJ's own
The four Input params mirror the form. There is deliberately no ParticipantID or LinkTo param: who
gets attached is the service's decision from the deal, not the browser's to assert.

fields.Name: Log Activity
fields.Description: Log one activity against a deal — a call, meeting, note or email — writing the Activity and its links in a single transaction, with the deal's account and primary contact attached as participants. The canonical composition; the deal workspace calls this rather than writing rows itself.
fields.UserPrompt: Log an activity against a deal.

fields.Name: DealID
fields.Description: The deal the activity is about. Always linked, always with role Regarding — it is the anchor every read of a deal's timeline starts from, so an activity without it would be unreachable rather than merely unattributed.

fields.Name: TypeCode
fields.Description: One of Call, Meeting, Note, Email — the ActivityType Code, never its display Name. Validated against that set rather than passed through, so a bad value is reported as a bad request instead of surfacing as 'no ActivityType with Code X', which reads like a missing seed.

fields.Name: Title
fields.Description: The subject. Activity.Title is NOT NULL, nvarchar(500).

fields.Name: StartedAt
fields.Description: When it happened, ISO-8601. Omit for now. An unparseable value is REFUSED rather than defaulted to the current time: a timeline is ordered by StartedAt, so a silent fallback files the activity at the wrong point with nothing to show it moved.
